sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ hṛṣṭāḥ saṃpūjayām āsuḥ pārtham akliṣṭakāriṇam
english: Then the gods together with gandharvas, the siddhas and the great sages, filled with joy, honoured Pārtha, the effortless doer.

sanskrit: āśīrvādaiḥ stūyamāno divyavāditranisvanaiḥ pratipede mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhadundubhināditam
english: Praised with blessings and the sounds of celestial instruments, the mighty-armed one entered the city resounding with conches and kettledrums.

sanskrit: nakṣatramārgaṃ vipulaṃ suravīthīti viśrutam indrājñayā yayau pārthaḥ stūyamānaḥ samantataḥ
english: By Indra's command Pārtha travelled the vast stellar path, known as the celestial highway, praised on all sides.

sanskrit: tatra sādhyās tathā viśve maruto 'thāśvināv api ādityā vasavo rudrās tathā brahmarṣayo 'malāḥ
english: There were the Sādhyas and the Viśvas, the Maruts and the twin Aśvins, the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, and the pure brahmarṣis.

sanskrit: rājarṣayaś ca bahavo dilīpapramukhā nṛpāḥ tumburur nāradaś caiva gandharvau ca hahāhuhū
english: Many royal sages and kings headed by Dilīpa were there, as were Tumburu and Nārada and the gandharvas Hāhā and Hūhū.

sanskrit: tān sarvān sa samāgamya vidhivat kurunandanaḥ tato 'paśyad devarājaṃ śatakratum ariṃdamam
english: After meeting all of them duly, the joy of the Kurus then beheld the king of gods, Śatakratu, the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho mahābāhur avatīrya rathottamāt dadarśa sākṣād devendraṃ pitaraṃ pākaśāsanam
english: Then mighty-armed Pārtha, descending from his excellent chariot, beheld face to face the lord of gods, his father Pākaśāsana.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa hemadaṇḍena cāruṇā divyagandhādhivāsena vyajanena vidhūyatā
english: — Indra, shaded by a white parasol with a beautiful golden handle, fanned by a whisk suffused with divine fragrance,

sanskrit: viśvāvasuprabhṛtibhir gandharvaiḥ stutivandanaiḥ stūyamānaṃ dvijāgryaiś ca ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃstavaiḥ
english: praised with hymns of homage by Viśvāvasu and other gandharvas, and lauded by the best of twice-born with recitations of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman.

sanskrit: tato 'bhigamya kaunteyaḥ śirasābhyanamad balī sa cainam anuvṛttābhyāṃ bhujābhyāṃ pratyagṛhṇata
english: Then the mighty son of Kuntī approached and bowed his head; and Indra received him with arms outstretched in affection.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakrāsane puṇye devarājarṣipūjite śakraḥ pāṇau gṛhītvainam upāveśayad antike
english: Then on that holy throne of Śakra, honoured by gods, kings and sages, Śakra took him by the hand and seated him close beside him.

sanskrit: mūrdhni cainam upāghrāya devendraḥ paravīrahā aṅkam āropayām āsa praśrayāvanataṃ tadā
english: And the lord of gods, slayer of enemy heroes, smelled his head and then, as he bowed humbly, placed him upon his own lap.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣaniyogāt sa pārthaḥ śakrāsanaṃ tadā adhyakrāmad ameyātmā dvitīya iva vāsavaḥ
english: At the behest of the Thousand-eyed one, Pārtha, that immeasurable soul, mounted Śakra's throne like a second Vāsava.

sanskrit: tataḥ premṇā vṛtraśatrur arjunasya śubhaṃ mukham pasparśa puṇyagandhena kareṇa parisāntvayan
english: Then the slayer of Vṛtra, filled with love, tenderly stroked Arjuna's fair face with his hand fragrant with sacred scent.

sanskrit: parimārjamānaḥ śanakair bāhū cāsyāyatau śubhau jyāśarakṣepakaṭhinau stambhāv iva hiraṇmayau
english: He gently stroked those two long, beautiful arms of his, hardened by the snap of the bowstring and the casting of arrows, like two golden pillars.

sanskrit: vajragrahaṇacihnena kareṇa balasūdanaḥ muhur muhur vajradharo bāhū saṃsphālayañ śanaiḥ
english: The slayer of Bala, the wielder of the thunderbolt, with the hand that bore the marks of the vajra's grip, patted those arms again and again, gently.

sanskrit: smayann iva guḍākeśaṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasradṛk harṣeṇotphullanayano na cātṛpyata vṛtrahā
english: The Thousand-eyed one gazed upon Guḍākeśa as if smiling, his eyes wide with delight; the slayer of Vṛtra could not have his fill.

sanskrit: ekāsanopaviṣṭau tau śobhayāṃ cakratuḥ sabhām sūryācandramasau vyomni caturdaśyām ivoditau
english: Seated together on one throne, those two glorified the assembly hall as the sun and moon rising in the sky on the fourteenth day.

sanskrit: tatra sma gāthā gāyanti sāmnā paramavalgunā gandharvās tumburuśreṣṭhāḥ kuśalā gītasāmasu
english: There the gandharvas, foremost of whom was Tumburu, skilled in song and sāman, sang ballads with the most beautiful melody.

sanskrit: ghṛtācī menakā rambhā pūrvacittiḥ svayaṃprabhā urvaśī miśrakeśī ca ḍuṇḍur gaurī varūthinī
english: Ghṛtācī, Menakā, Rambhā, Pūrvacitti, Svayaṃprabhā, Urvaśī, Miśrakeśī, Ḍuṇḍu, Gaurī, and Varūthinī —

sanskrit: gopālī sahajanyā ca kumbhayoniḥ prajāgarā citrasenā citralekhā sahā ca madhurasvarā
english: Gopālī, Sahajanyā, Kumbhayoni, Prajāgarā, Citrasena, Citralekhā, Sahā, and the sweet-voiced one —

sanskrit: etāś cānyāś ca nanṛtus tatra tatra varāṅganāḥ cittapramathane yuktāḥ siddhānāṃ padmalocanāḥ
english: these and other beautiful women, lotus-eyed, devoted to stirring the hearts of the siddhas, danced here and there.

sanskrit: mahākaṭitaṭaśroṇyaḥ kampamānaiḥ payodharaiḥ kaṭākṣahāvamādhuryaiś cetobuddhimanoharāḥ
english: With broad hips and full flanks, their breasts trembling, with the sweetness of their sidelong glances and coquetry, they captivated the heart, mind and intellect.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ samādāyārghyam uttamam śakrasya matam ājñāya pārtham ānarcur añjasā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the gods together with gandharvas, taking the finest guest-offering and acting on Śakra's pleasure, honoured Pārtha straightway.

sanskrit: pādyam ācamanīyaṃ ca pratigrāhya nṛpātmajam praveśayām āsur atho puraṃdaraniveśanam
english: Presenting water for the feet and water for rinsing the mouth to the prince and receiving them back, they then led him into the dwelling of Purandara.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃpūjito jiṣṇur uvāsa bhavane pituḥ upaśikṣan mahāstrāṇi sasaṃhārāṇi pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Honoured thus, the victorious Pāṇḍava dwelt in his father's abode, learning the great weapons together with their methods of withdrawal.

sanskrit: śakrasya hastād dayitaṃ vajram astraṃ durutsaham aśanīś ca mahānādā meghabarhiṇalakṣaṇāḥ
english: From Śakra's own hand he received the beloved, irresistible weapon the vajra, and the thunderbolts of great roar bearing the mark of cloud and peacock.

sanskrit: gṛhītāstras tu kaunteyo bhrātṝn sasmāra pāṇḍavaḥ puraṃdaraniyogāc ca pañcābdam avasat sukhī
english: Having received the weapons, the son of Kuntī, the Pāṇḍava, remembered his brothers; yet by Purandara's command he dwelt there happily for five years.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakro 'bravīt pārthaṃ kṛtāstraṃ kāla āgate nṛttaṃ gītaṃ ca kaunteya citrasenād avāpnuhi
english: Then, when the time had come, Śakra said to Pārtha who had mastered the weapons: 'O son of Kuntī, now learn dance and music from Citrasena.'

sanskrit: vāditraṃ devavihitaṃ nṛloke yan na vidyate tad arjayasva kaunteya śreyo vai te bhaviṣyati
english: 'Acquire the music ordained by the gods, which does not exist in the mortal world, O son of Kuntī — it will be for your benefit.'

sanskrit: sakhāyaṃ pradadau cāsya citrasenaṃ puraṃdaraḥ sa tena saha saṃgamya reme pārtho nirāmayaḥ
english: Purandara gave him Citrasena as a companion; and Pārtha, free from all affliction, spent his time joyfully with him.

sanskrit: kadā cid aṭamānas tu maharṣir uta lomaśaḥ jagāma śakrabhavanaṃ puraṃdaradidṛkṣayā
english: Now one day, as the great sage Lomaśa happened to be wandering about, he went to the abode of Śakra desiring to see Purandara.

sanskrit: sa sametya namaskṛtya devarājaṃ mahāmuniḥ dadarśārdhāsanagataṃ pāṇḍavaṃ vāsavasya ha
english: That great sage, having met and saluted the king of gods, saw the Pāṇḍava seated on a half-share of Vāsava's throne.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakrābhyanujñāta āsane viṣṭarottare niṣasāda dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ pūjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
english: Then, permitted by Śakra, the best of twice-born took his seat on an elevated cushioned seat, honoured by the great sages.

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvābhavad buddhiḥ pārtham indrāsane sthitam kathaṃ nu kṣatriyaḥ pārthaḥ śakrāsanam avāptavān
english: Having seen him, the thought arose in his mind: how has Pārtha, a kṣatriya, come to occupy Śakra's throne?

sanskrit: kiṃ tv asya sukṛtaṃ karma lokā vā ke vinirjitāḥ ya evam upasaṃprāptaḥ sthānaṃ devanamaskṛtam
english: What meritorious deed has he done, or what worlds has he conquered, that he has attained this station revered by the gods?

sanskrit: tasya vijñāya saṃkalpaṃ śakro vṛtraniṣūdanaḥ lomaśaṃ prahasan vākyam idam āha śacīpatiḥ
english: Perceiving his thought, Śakra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of Śacī, spoke these words to Lomaśa with a smile.

sanskrit: brahmarṣe śrūyatāṃ yat te manasaitad vivakṣitam nāyaṃ kevalamartyo vai kṣatriyatvam upāgataḥ
english: 'O brahmarṣi, let what you wish to say in your heart be heard — this one is not a mere mortal who has taken on the state of a kṣatriya.

sanskrit: maharṣe mama putro 'yaṃ kuntyāṃ jāto mahābhujaḥ astrahetor iha prāptaḥ kasmāc cit kāraṇāntarāt
english: O great sage, this mighty-armed one born of Kuntī is my son; he has come here for weapons, and also for another reason.

sanskrit: aho nainaṃ bhavān vetti purāṇam ṛṣisattamam śṛṇu me vadato brahman yo 'yaṃ yac cāsya kāraṇam
english: Ah, you do not know this ancient one, O best of sages. Listen as I tell you, O brahman, who he truly is and what his purpose is.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇau yau tau purāṇāv ṛṣisattamau tāv imāv abhijānīhi hṛṣīkeśadhanaṃjayau
english: Those two ancient ones, the best of sages — Nara and Nārāyaṇa — know them to be these two: Hṛṣīkeśa and Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: yan na śakyaṃ surair draṣṭum ṛṣibhir vā mahātmabhiḥ tad āśramapadaṃ puṇyaṃ badarī nāma viśrutam
english: That holy hermitage, known by the name Badarī, which cannot be seen by gods or great-souled sages —

sanskrit: sa nivāso 'bhavad vipra viṣṇor jiṣṇos tathaiva ca yataḥ pravavṛte gaṅgā siddhacāraṇasevitā
english: that, O brahman, was the abode of Viṣṇu as well as of Jiṣṇu, from whence flows the Gaṅgā frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas.

sanskrit: tau manniyogād brahmarṣe kṣitau jātau mahādyutī bhūmer bhārāvataraṇaṃ mahāvīryau kariṣyataḥ
english: Those two of great splendour, O brahmarṣi, have been born on earth at my behest; possessed of great valour, they will accomplish the lightening of earth's burden.

sanskrit: udvṛttā hy asurāḥ ke cin nivātakavacā iti vipriyeṣu sthitāsmākaṃ varadānena mohitāḥ
english: For certain arrogant asuras called Nivātakavacas, deluded by the boon they have received, remain set against our welfare.

sanskrit: tarkayante surān hantuṃ baladarpasamanvitāḥ devān na gaṇayante ca tathā dattavarā hi te
english: Puffed up with the pride of their strength, they plot to slay the gods and count the gods as nothing — such is the boon they have been granted.

sanskrit: pātālavāsino raudrā danoḥ putrā mahābalāḥ sarve devanikāyā hi nālaṃ yodhayituṃ sma tān
english: These terrible, mighty sons of Danu dwelling in the netherworld — all the hosts of gods together are not capable of fighting them.

sanskrit: yo 'sau bhūmigataḥ śrīmān viṣṇur madhuniṣūdanaḥ kapilo nāma devo 'sau bhagavān ajito hariḥ
english: He who has descended to the earth, glorious Viṣṇu, slayer of Madhu — that is the deity known as Kapila, the blessed, unconquered Hari.

sanskrit: yena pūrvaṃ mahātmānaḥ khanamānā rasātalam darśanād eva nihatāḥ sagarasyātmajā vibho
english: By whose mere glance, O mighty one, the great-souled sons of Sagara, digging down to the netherworld, were slain in former times.

sanskrit: tena kāryaṃ mahat kāryam asmākaṃ dvijasattama pārthena ca mahāyuddhe sametābhyām asaṃśayam
english: A great task must be accomplished for us by both of them together in a mighty battle — by him and by Pārtha — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: ayaṃ teṣāṃ samastānāṃ śaktaḥ pratisamāsane tān nihatya raṇe śūraḥ punar yāsyati mānuṣān
english: This one is capable of facing all of them; having slain them in battle, the hero will return to the world of men.

sanskrit: bhavāṃś cāsmanniyogena yātu tāvan mahītalam kāmyake drakṣyase vīraṃ nivasantaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: And you, at our behest, go now to the earth — in the Kāmyaka forest you will see the hero Yudhiṣṭhira dwelling there.

sanskrit: sa vācyo mama saṃdeśād dharmātmā satyasaṃgaraḥ notkaṇṭhā phalgune kāryā kṛtāstraḥ śīghram eṣyati
english: Tell that righteous soul, firm in truth, with this message from me: no anxiety need be felt on account of Phalguna — he has mastered the weapons and will come soon.

sanskrit: nāśuddhabāhuvīryeṇa nākṛtāstreṇa vā raṇe bhīṣmadroṇādayo yuddhe śakyāḥ pratisamāsitum
english: Without the pure strength of his arms and without mastery of weapons, it is not possible to stand against Bhīṣma, Droṇa and the others in battle.

sanskrit: gṛhītāstro guḍākeśo mahābāhur mahāmanāḥ nṛttavāditragītānāṃ divyānāṃ pāram eyivān
english: Guḍākeśa, mighty-armed and great-souled, having received the weapons, has also reached the mastery of divine dance, instrumental music, and song.

sanskrit: bhavān api viviktāni tīrthāni manujeśvara bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvair draṣṭum arhaty ariṃdama
english: You too, O lord of men, subduer of foes, deserve to visit the sacred tīrthas in seclusion together with all your brothers.

sanskrit: tīrtheṣv āplutya puṇyeṣu vipāpmā vigatajvaraḥ rājyaṃ bhokṣyasi rājendra sukhī vigatakalmaṣaḥ
english: Having bathed at the holy tīrthas, freed from sin and released from affliction, you will enjoy the kingdom, O king of kings, happy and cleansed of all taint.

sanskrit: bhavāṃś cainaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha paryaṭantaṃ mahītale trātum arhati viprāgrya tapobalasamanvitaḥ
english: And you, O best of twice-born, foremost of brahmans, endowed with the power of your austerities, should protect him as he wanders across the earth.

sanskrit: giridurgeṣu hi sadā deśeṣu viṣameṣu ca vasanti rākṣasā raudrās tebhyo rakṣet sadā bhavān
english: For in the mountain fastnesses and in rough terrain, terrible rākṣasas always dwell — from them may you always guard him.

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratijñāya lomaśaḥ sumahātapāḥ kāmyakaṃ vanam uddiśya samupāyān mahītalam
english: Lomaśa of great austerity, having promised 'so be it,' descended to the earth directing his course to the Kāmyaka forest.

sanskrit: dadarśa tatra kaunteyaṃ dharmarājam ariṃdamam tāpasair bhrātṛbhiś caiva sarvataḥ parivāritam
english: There he saw the son of Kuntī, the righteous king, subduer of foes, surrounded on all sides by ascetics and his brothers.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca atyadbhutam idaṃ karma pārthasyāmitatejasaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭro mahātejāḥ śrutvā vipra kim abravīt
english: Janamejaya said: This deed of Pārtha of boundless splendour is most wondrous — what did the great-spirited Dhṛtarāṣṭra say, O brahman, upon hearing it?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śakralokagataṃ pārthaṃ śrutvā rājāmbikāsutaḥ dvaipāyanād ṛṣiśreṣṭhāt saṃjayaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard that Pārtha had gone to Śakra's world, the king, son of Ambikā, spoke these words to Saṃjaya through the foremost of sages, Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ me sūta kārtsnyena karma pārthasya dhīmataḥ kaccit tavāpi viditaṃ yathātathyena sārathe
english: 'I have heard the complete account of the wise Pārtha's deed — do you too know it accurately as it truly is, O charioteer?'

sanskrit: pramatto grāmyadharmeṣu mandātmā pāpaniścayaḥ mama putraḥ sudurbuddhiḥ pṛthivīṃ ghātayiṣyati
english: 'My son, heedless, devoted to base pleasures, dull-minded, fixed on evil, utterly foolish of understanding, will bring destruction upon the earth.'

sanskrit: yasya nityam ṛtā vācaḥ svaireṣv api mahātmanaḥ trailokyam api tasya syād yoddhā yasya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: 'Even the words of that great-souled one are ever true even in casual speech — even the three worlds would belong to one whose warrior is Dhanaṃjaya.'

sanskrit: asyataḥ karṇinārācāṃs tīkṣṇāgrāṃś ca śilāśitān ko 'rjunasyāgratas tiṣṭhed api mṛtyur jarātigaḥ
english: 'As he releases his feathered arrows and sharp iron shafts whetted on stone, who could stand before Arjuna — not even Death that surpasses old age?'

sanskrit: mama putrā durātmānaḥ sarve mṛtyuvaśaṃ gatāḥ yeṣāṃ yuddhaṃ durādharṣaiḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ pratyupasthitam
english: 'My wicked sons have all gone under death's dominion, against whom battle with the formidable Pāṇḍavas now looms.'

sanskrit: tasyaiva ca na paśyāmi yudhi gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ aniśaṃ cintayāno 'pi ya enam udiyād rathī
english: 'Even thinking constantly, I see no chariot-warrior who could rise up against the wielder of Gāṇḍīva in battle.'

sanskrit: droṇakarṇau pratīyātāṃ yadi bhīṣmo 'pi vā raṇe mahān syāt saṃśayo loke na tu paśyāmi no jayam
english: 'Even if Droṇa and Karṇa were to face him, or even Bhīṣma in battle, there would be great uncertainty in the world — yet I see no victory for us.'

sanskrit: ghṛṇī karṇaḥ pramādī ca ācāryaḥ sthaviro guruḥ amarṣī balavān pārthaḥ saṃrambhī dṛḍhavikramaḥ
english: 'Karṇa is compassionate and careless, the teacher is old and venerable, while Pārtha is wrathful, powerful, fierce and of firm valour.'

sanskrit: bhavet sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ sarvaśo 'py aparājitam sarve hy astravidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve prāptā mahad yaśaḥ
english: 'There would be a most tumultuous battle, unconquered on all sides — for all are versed in weapons, all are heroes, all have won great glory.'

sanskrit: api sarveśvaratvaṃ hi na vāñcheran parājitāḥ vadhe nūnaṃ bhavec chāntis teṣāṃ vā phalgunasya vā
english: 'Even were they defeated, they would not desire sovereignty over everything — only in the death of them or of Phalguna would there certainly be peace.'

sanskrit: na tu hantārjunasyāsti jetā vāsya na vidyate manyus tasya kathaṃ śāmyen mandān prati samutthitaḥ
english: 'Yet there is no slayer of Arjuna, no conqueror of him exists — how could his rage be appeased, risen as it is against these base ones?'

sanskrit: tridaśeśasamo vīraḥ khāṇḍave 'gnim atarpayat jigāya pārthivān sarvān rājasūye mahākratau
english: 'Equal to the lord of the thirty gods, the hero satisfied Agni in the Khāṇḍava forest and conquered all kings at the great Rājasūya sacrifice.'

sanskrit: śeṣaṃ kuryād girer vajraṃ nipatan mūrdhni saṃjaya na tu kuryuḥ śarāḥ śeṣam astās tāta kirīṭinā
english: 'A thunderbolt falling on a mountain's peak might leave some remnant, O Saṃjaya — but the arrows and weapons shot by the Diademed one, my son, would leave nothing.'

sanskrit: yathā hi kiraṇā bhānos tapantīha carācaram tathā pārthabhujotsṛṣṭāḥ śarās tapsyanti me sutān
english: 'Just as the rays of the sun scorch all that moves and is still, so the arrows released from Pārtha's arm will scorch my sons.'

sanskrit: api vā rathaghoṣeṇa bhayārtā savyasācinaḥ pratibhāti vidīrṇeva sarvato bhāratī camūḥ
english: 'Or even by the din of the chariot of Savyasācin, the entire Bhārata army appears to me as if shattered in every direction, stricken with terror.'

sanskrit: yad udvapan pravapaṃś caiva bāṇān; sthātātatāyī samare kirīṭī sṛṣṭo 'ntakaḥ sarvaharo vidhātrā; bhaved yathā tadvad apāraṇīyaḥ
english: 'As he stands discharging and raining down arrows in battle — Kirīṭī, the aggressor — like Death sent forth by Fate to take all, he would be unstoppable.'

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yad etat kathitaṃ rājaṃs tvayā duryodhanaṃ prati sarvam etad yathāttha tvaṃ naitan mithyā mahīpate
english: Saṃjaya said: What you have declared here, O king, regarding Duryodhana — all of it is exactly as you say; this is not false, O lord of the earth.
